title: Sharada Tilaka Tantra (Laxmanacharya)
shelf_note: Śāradātilaka, a core Śākta/Tantric ritual manual, Sanskrit text only in Devanagari print.
structure_note: Pages 1-291 with OCR and translation on every page. The 59 backsteps and 69 repeats look like misread page numerals: on leaf 222 the printed number is २१९ but the OCR records 214 and also writes a 'विंशः पटलः । २१४' line that is not on the page. The 'published 1100' field gives the date of composition, not of this printed edition.

syllables dropped in two words
conjunct misread

tr_errors.source: ततः शम्भोर्दिशि गुरुर्विकिरेत् पूर्वसञ्चिते । हेमवस्त्रादिसंयुक्तां कर्क्करीं तोयपूरिताम्
tr_errors.english: the teacher should scatter [water] from a vessel filled with water, decorated with gold and cloth
tr_errors.problem: two clauses merged: the 'vikira' grains are scattered on what was gathered earlier, and the water pot is set up as a separate act (continued in 124). The English makes it one act of scattering water.

tr_errors.english: protecting it with water released from the palms, as is done for the guardians of the directions
tr_errors.problem: 'nāla' is the spout of the pot, not the palms; and 'rakṣa' is a command spoken to the lokapālas ('protect!'), not something the teacher does

tr_errors.source: ततश्च संहते वह्नौ गोक्षीरेण चं पचेत्

tr_errors.problem: the object 'caru' is missing (the OCR dropped it) and 'combined fire' is too literal

other.note: the translation opens with '# Fourth Chapter', a heading that is not on the page (the running head reads सारदातिलकम्)

tr_errors.problem: the source says the rite makes [people] subject to the practitioner. 'Makes the invisible visible' is invented from the OCR misreading.

tr_errors.english: he becomes like a master of all beings
tr_errors.problem: the source says all beings become subject to him. The English is a paraphrase built on a garbled word.

'mṛga' (the deer in the moon's lap) lost
half-line garbled

tr_errors.problem: a fluent sentence written over garbled OCR, with no sign that the source is uncertain

tr_errors.english: a six-syllable mantra: "Om to Soma." <note>original: "Om Somāya namah"</note>
tr_errors.problem: the note supplies a mantra the page does not give. The verse encodes the bīja (sauṃ) and the note substitutes 'Om'; the 'Bhrigu = śa' gloss is also wrong (bhṛgu = sa).

tr_errors.english: who has the qualities of the support of the gods in his own lap
tr_errors.problem: this should be the deer in his lap (from the OCR misreading)

ocr_errors.image: printed page २१९; no such line in the body
ocr_errors.problem: page number misread, and a running-head line is added to the body that is not on the page

'Aghora is its seer' becomes 'the seer of Aghora'
the epithet is misread
misread

tr_errors.problem: the verse numbers are shifted by one against the text throughout, so a citation by verse number points to the wrong verse

tr_errors.english: with the five cruel ones mixed with fat and ghee
tr_errors.problem: the source reads 'andhasā' (with food), which the OCR misread as 'vasā' (fat)

tr_errors.problem: the source names Aghora as the seer; the English leaves the seer unnamed

other.note: the translation repeats 'Twentieth Chapter. 214' as body text under a '# Twentieth Chapter.' heading, and the 214 is a wrong number

book_verdict: The right text on every page and a broadly accurate translation of a ritual manual, but each page has several meaning-changing OCR misreadings that the English carries forward fluently. One of them invents a magical effect ('makes the invisible visible') that the text does not state.
reader_summary: This is the Sanskrit text of the Śāradātilaka, a medieval Tantric manual of mantra rites, transcribed from a printed Devanagari edition. The transcription is of the right text but drops or misreads several syllables per page. The English follows the ritual sequence correctly but repeats those misreadings, mixes up some technical terms, and shifts verse numbers on some pages, so it should be checked against the Sanskrit before anyone quotes it.

title: Tantraloka Vol. 1 with Jayaratha Commentary
shelf_note: Abhinavagupta's Tantrāloka with Jayaratha's Viveka, Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies edition (1918), from a Toronto copy.
structure_note: Leaf 211 is printed p.201 (Āhnika 1, verse 166), but leaf 348 is printed p.26 with verses 31-32 of a later āhnika. A second pagination sequence therefore begins in the last part of the scan, probably the next volume bound with this one. The title 'Vol. 1' covers only part of the scan. The 28 backsteps fit this restart plus misread numerals. 368 of 372 pages have OCR, but pages_translated_field is 359 against 368 counted.

syllable lost

tr_errors.problem: the running head is rendered as a section heading

ocr_errors.problem: a printed verse numeral silently corrected toward the expected number

tr_errors.english: if it is manifest, it is already part of the Light; if it is unmanifest, it is nothing at all
tr_errors.problem: explanatory expansion added without brackets

other.note: the translation has a '### Light on the Tantras' heading followed by raw <page-num>172</page-num><header>…</header> tags in the text

tr_errors.source: अभावात् को नाम फलभूतेऽपि मोक्षे भेदः स्यात्
tr_errors.english: ...en universal Consciousness? Therefore, since there is no difference in the underlying reality, what possible difference...
tr_errors.problem: the translation opens with a word fragment and a clause carried over from the previous page

tr_errors.english: for those whose mental fluctuations have settled into a state of pure stillness
tr_errors.problem: this word is the tail of a compound split across the page (probably nirvikalpa-), and the English guesses a meaning for the whole without saying so

other.note: the running head is rendered as '# The Holy Tantrāloka #', and raw <page-num>/<header> tags appear in the translation

book_verdict: Clean transcriptions of a clearly printed edition and careful English with useful terms. The defects are display furniture (headings, leaked tags) and one carry-over fragment from the previous page.
reader_summary: This is the Sanskrit Tantrāloka of Abhinavagupta with Jayaratha's commentary, in the 1918 Kashmir Series edition. The transcription matches the printed page almost word for word, and the English renders both verse and commentary faithfully, including the editor's variant-reading notes. Warn the reader that the reader text carries stray headings and tags, and that the scan seems to continue into a second volume with its own page numbers.

title: Paramesvaratantra
shelf_note: An early Nepalese palm-leaf manuscript of a Śaiva tantra (Cambridge). It belongs on the shelf.
structure_note: 124 single palm leaves photographed with a ruler and no foliation recorded. The OCR page numbers come from leaf numerals in the margin (e.g. 56 on leaf 112), which explains the many backsteps and repeats. All 124 leaves are 'translated' even though the OCR is mostly unreadable.

ocr_errors.image: five lines in three blocks, in early Nepalese (pre-Newari) script
ocr_errors.problem: a few strings match the leaf (e.g. 'कथा गाथ' at the end of line 1, 'कुर्याद्' in line 3), but most of the text is garbled or filled in with plausible Sanskrit that is not on the leaf

tr_errors.english: the ballad of the merchant… Know the Garuda-lore… eight hundred mantras
tr_errors.problem: fluent English, glossed themes and a summary are built on an OCR that is mostly not the leaf's text. Ellipses mark some gaps, but the summary states the leaf's content as fact.

other.note: the <summary> invents a confident description ('a collection of eight hundred mantras used to provide protection against serpents')

ocr_errors.image: a litany of '… नमोऽस्तु', 'शिवाय नमोऽस्तु', 'व्याधि …' formulas; I could not find 'सायुज्य' in the readable middle block
ocr_errors.problem: a repeated formula ('may there be union') appears to be invented and imposed on the leaf

tr_errors.english: May there be union with Shiva… union through divine presence
tr_errors.problem: the page's theme as translated ('sāyujya', liberation by union) rests on a word that does not appear to be on the leaf

other.note: the <meta> refers to the previous page's metadata suggesting 'Mahayana Buddhist themes': model commentary on its own earlier output

ocr_errors.image: line 1 of the left block, which is main text (roughly '…शिवः प्रश्ना… शिवा… विना…')
ocr_errors.problem: a line of main text is replaced by an invented 'gloss' about the Sāvitrī mantra
the rest is garbled or confabulated

tr_errors.english: # The Ritual of the Teacher's Armor … the son of the protector of the gods is capable of forgiveness … even unto the Cremation Ground
tr_errors.problem: connected English 'meaning' is made from non-text; it is not a translation of this leaf

other.note: an invented heading '# The Ritual of the Teacher's Armor'; the <meta> claims the previous page began a 'Kavacha'

ocr_errors.image: five-line palm leaf with leaf number 56 in the margin
ocr_errors.problem: the leaf number and a few words ('दीक्षा', 'गरुड') match; most of the transcription is garbled, and the bīja mantra 'श्री ह्रीं भद्रकाली ह्रीं नमः' could not be found on the leaf

tr_errors.english: protective rituals… centered on the goddess Bhadrakali and the twelve Rudras
tr_errors.problem: a confident summary and theme built on unreliable OCR, and the notes guess at the meaning of non-words ('madidyāsākā, likely vidyā-sādhaka')

book_verdict: A precious early palm-leaf manuscript whose script the OCR cannot read. Each leaf's transcription is mostly garbage or invented Sanskrit, and the English presents confident ritual content built on it.
reader_summary: The images are of a very early Nepalese palm-leaf manuscript of the Parameśvaratantra, which is valuable in itself. The transcription is not a reading of these leaves: only scattered words match, and the rest is garbled or plausible Sanskrit made up to fill the gaps. The English and its summaries therefore describe contents the leaves may not contain and cannot be trusted. Show the images only.

title: Rig-Veda-Sanhita: Sacred Hymns of the Brahmans (Vol. 3)
shelf_note: Max Müller's editio princeps of the Ṛgveda with Sāyaṇa's commentary, Vol. III (Maṇḍalas 5-7). The footer reads 'VOL. III.'
structure_note: Pages run in order (309, 623, 922 at leaves 375, 691, 990), with 1,058 of 1,062 pages OCR'd. The 101 backsteps and 134 repeats are probably the Devanagari page numbers misread, or the Ashtaka/Adhyāya numbers in the running heads taken as page numbers; none showed in this sample. pages_translated_field is 1049 against 1058 counted.

other.note: the OCR of a blank flyleaf carries template headings ('## Hymn Text [Blank Page]', '## Commentary (Sayana) [Blank Page]')

tr_errors.english: Agni has surpassed the immortals by his wisdom
tr_errors.problem: Sāyaṇa takes 'atārīt' as 'carried the gods across / saved them', not 'surpassed', which changes Agni's relation to the gods

tr_errors.source: अरणस्यानृणस्य रेक्णो धनं परिषद्यं पर्याप्तं भवति हि
tr_errors.english: The wealth of a stranger… is to be avoided or is merely something that surrounds us
tr_errors.problem: Sāyaṇa's first gloss says 'pariṣadyam = sufficient/abundant'. The English gives the alternative gloss ('to be avoided') as the first reading.

book_verdict: An accurate transcription of a cleanly printed Vedic edition, with a careful, useful English rendering of hymn and Sāyaṇa. A few glosses slip, and model furniture (headings, vocab blocks) is added to the reader text.
reader_summary: This is Max Müller's printed Ṛgveda with Sāyaṇa's commentary, Volume III, with saṃhitā text, pada-pāṭha and commentary transcribed almost exactly. The English follows Sāyaṇa closely and is mostly reliable, though a few of his glosses are misrendered. The reader text also carries headings and glossary blocks that are not in the book.
